title: Hazel and the Border
premise: Isandro Eriksen, a financial-crimes investigator who entered witness protection after exposing a laundering network spanning three governments, discovers the safe house he's hidden in for three years has been listed online — interior photos and all — meaning someone inside the program sold him out. As he races to move a decrypted ledger proving which officials took the money, an assassin named Hazel closes in, but she carries her own inheritance: her father was one of the men Isandro's evidence would destroy. In the end, Isandro gets the ledger to a journalist by sacrificing his anonymity entirely, while Hazel chooses to burn her father's legacy rather than protect it, leaving both of them exposed but finally free.
about_author: Sable Villalobos is the pen name of a former compliance analyst who spent a decade tracing money through shell companies before turning to fiction. They write thrillers about ordinary people trapped inside systems designed to forget them.

chapters.title: The Listing
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Scrolling property sites out of boredom, he finds his own safe house listed with photos showing his books, his coffee mug, his life. His handler dismisses it as a database error, but that night the listing vanishes and his dead-drop goes cold. The emotional beat is the vertigo of realizing invisibility was always an illusion — someone has been watching, cataloguing, waiting.

chapters.title: Hazel Arrives
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Isandro flees to a second location while Hazel, the assassin hired through laundered channels, studies childhood photos of her father beside the very officials named in Isandro's ledger. She's been told the target is a liar; the file says otherwise. The beat is dread doubling into doubt — hunter and hunted each discovering the other may be the only honest person left.

chapters.title: Three Governments, One Truth
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV, with a tense midpoint scene from Hazel's. Isandro tries to hand the ledger to prosecutors in two countries and is stonewalled both times — names redacted, meetings cancelled, one contact arrested within hours. He realizes the corruption reaches the protection program itself. The beat is claustrophobic betrayal: every door meant to save him opens inward toward the wolves.

chapters.title: The Border
chapters.summary: Dual POV converging at a border crossing where Hazel corners Isandro but finds her father's signature in the ledger's margins. Climax: she lets him pass and destroys the kill order, then leaks the ledger herself when Isandro's escape route collapses. Resolution: his testimony goes public, his old identity dies, and two strangers meet once more — unhidden, unowned, on the line between pasts they've burned.
